game_total_and_team_total.existing_mechanism: Expected goals for each team equal shot volume times shot quality times goalie conversion, with an additive special-teams component from expected penalties and an empty-net component from late close-game dynamics. Thresholds at integer and half-goal rungs price tail probabilities requiring dispersion estimates.

goalie_saves.existing_mechanism: Saves equal shots on goal faced minus goals against, so the mean is the opponent's expected SOG against this defence adjusted for script, penalties and rink counting. Goalie quality only matters at the margin (a few shots), while volume matters most. The largest tail risks are an early pull (truncating saves) and goalie identity uncertainty before confirmation; overtime adds shots if included.

Third-period outcomes are a mixture over entering score state; the pregame win probability interacts with pull timing and score-effect shot rates.
First-period goals rely on starting units against the starting goalie, so the interaction of opening deployments and goalie quality is more informative than full-game averages.
Second-period scoring: long change effect interacts with line-shuffle tendencies and team skating depth.

period_markets.existing_mechanism: A period is a short sample from the full-game process with period-specific shape: low-event first periods, long-change second periods and score-state-dominated third periods. Since few goals occur (few per period) the distribution is dominated by zeros and ones and ties are common, so winner markets are heavily affected by tie-handling and the tail shape of Poisson-like counts. Goalie identity and first-minute deployments matter proportionally more than in the full game.

existing_interactions.hypothesis: PP minutes x PP point rate x opponent PK structure: expected PP production is the product of unit share of PP time, projected penalties drawn, and the PK concession pattern, not any one of them.
Assists = linemates' conversion x player's primary-assist rate; regress on-ice SH% before use, so linemate xG interacts with on-ice luck regression.
Goal probability = ixG-based chance volume x finishing x opponent goalie quality adjustments; goalie danger-split matters most for shooters of high-danger shots.
Multi-point thresholds are driven by team-level goal environment: team total and empty-net share raise the odds that the star is on ice for several goals.

player_points_goals_assists.existing_mechanism: Each goal is a Bernoulli outcome on every shot, so goals follow from shots x shot quality x finishing x opposing goalie; assists require being the passer on a teammate goal and so depend on linemates' finishing and on the player's playmaking role. Points are the union, so volume (TOI, especially PP1 time) dominates, while on-ice shooting luck is noise. The distribution is zero-heavy with thin tails, so thresholds above 1 need joint information on game total and team goals.

existing_interactions.hypothesis: Expected SOG = EV TOI x EV rate + PP TOI x PP rate; PP TOI is uncertain because it depends on the number of penalties drawn, so PP-heavy shooters have fatter right tails.
Block/miss conversion x shooter type: defencemen face higher block rates at the point and forwards' SOG depend on slot volume, so the opponent block rate has different effects by position.
Rink counting bias scales official SOG for both teams; adjust the player's rate by home/away venue factor, interacting with the player's home share.
Script x TOI: for a favoured team's star, leading late reduces minutes and shots; for an underdog star, trailing raises both.

player_shots_on_goal.existing_mechanism: Shots on goal result from TOI by state times attempt rate times the fraction of attempts that are not blocked or missed. Role differences are large: forwards in the slot, defencemen at the point and PP1 shooters generate shots at very different rates per minute, and the count is overdispersed because script, penalties and linemates change both volume and accuracy. Official counting varies by rink, so venue bias is a direct measurement effect on settlement.

unreg:team_and_player_season_counting.existing_mechanism: Season totals are games played times per-game rates, where rates depend on ice time, power-play role, linemates and shot quality, and games played depend on injury hazard. Over-dispersion and age curves matter; early-season to-date totals are weak evidence relative to talent priors.
